person.name: Mohamed Zaitoun
person.headline: Product engineering for merchant operations
person.intro: At Concentrix, I manage a rotating portfolio of 400+ DoorDash merchant accounts and lead the technical work on Merchant Success Hub. I built the portfolio views that help account managers choose which stores to approach and prepare outreach for those merchants.
about: People call me Zaitounish, a play on my surname and the word for olive. Before I managed merchant accounts, I sold online ordering and loyalty software to restaurant operators. Those conversations still shape the tools I build.

At Concentrix, I manage merchant accounts for DoorDash. I also lead the technical work on Merchant Success Hub. Earlier, I built language model applications at Augmentoria and studied data analysis through Udacity.

bullets: Manage a rotating portfolio of 400+ DoorDash merchant accounts, resolve operational issues and review progress against monthly and quarterly targets.
Built MSM Markup Tracker to replace manual pricing compliance reports. Markup sales grew 27% quarter over quarter and reached 133% of the quarterly target.
Built MSM Campaign Dispatcher to prepare tailored merchant campaigns in under 10 minutes. The tool contributed to a 17.9% increase in Concentrix vendor sales.
Reached 118% of sales quota selling online ordering, branded mobile apps and loyalty programs to restaurant operators.
Helped operators choose a setup for their business, from the first conversation through the close. Deal velocity improved by 20%.
Developed ArtifyAI v1.1, a text-to-image application. Fine-tuned Stable Diffusion on 5,000+ COCO images and integrated T5 to handle prompts in four languages.
Used MLflow and Hugging Face for experiment tracking and model versioning during a 177-hour AI and machine learning program.
Built and deployed 3+ language model applications with Python and LangChain for business tasks including data extraction and classification.
Built Gradio interfaces so colleagues could run the applications themselves and give feedback on the results.
Resolved 94% of technical issues on the first call across 1,000+ customer interactions. Maintained a 96% customer satisfaction rating.
Used Salesforce, VMware and Avaya to troubleshoot customer issues and record the resolution.

projects.name: Merchant Success Hub
projects.resumeDescription: Led engineering for Merchant Success Hub across multiple lines of business in Concentrix’s DoorDash program. Built portfolio filters and saved views for reps, with access tied to role and account assignment. Weekly reporting preserves sales credit when reps move between teams.
projects.summary: An account manager can filter for promotion opportunities, select stores and draft personalized emails directly from that list. A team lead can see which merchants still need outreach and help reps focus their time before month-end.
details: Built portfolio filtering and saved views for merchant teams across lines of business.
Account management’s weekly report compares approved sales claims with official results by product and credits sales to the team responsible at the time.

case.intro: A restaurant can have several locations, and the same store can have an account manager and a retention rep at the same time. We designed the Hub so each line of business can own its work with that merchant.
case.contribution: The Hub supports multiple lines of business, each with its own merchant goals. A missing menu photo gives an early merchant support rep a reason to reach out to a new restaurant. For a retention rep, success means helping an inactive store take orders again. Each team keeps ownership of its work, even when teams support the same merchant.

spotlight.title: Where should a sales lead step in?
paragraphs: Halfway through the month, two reps can be equally far from target for different reasons. One has spotted promotion opportunities but hasn’t contacted those merchants yet. The other has sales claims awaiting review.
One rep needs help choosing merchants to approach. The other needs a decision on work already submitted.

story.title: From a merchant list to a sales opportunity
paragraphs: Portfolios and targets lived in spreadsheets, campaign preparation happened in a separate tool, and weekly reviews meant reconciling what reps submitted with official sales figures. I built the Hub’s portfolio views around the question I faced as an account manager. Which merchant has a reason to hear from me today?

The work varies by line of business. An account manager can filter for promotion opportunities and draft personalized outreach for the stores they select. Early merchant support uses menu and promotion data to find gaps at new restaurants. Retention reps follow inactive stores through reactivation.

story.title: One store, different owners
paragraphs: In the Hub’s multi-tenant data model, each store has a separate assignment for each line of business that works with it. When a portfolio changes hands, dated assignments preserve who was responsible for the store before and after the transfer.

I built the portfolio filters and saved views in React so reps could keep the spreadsheet workflow they knew. Azure Functions and PostgreSQL enforce access by role, team and assignment. That gives a lead a view across their team’s accounts while each rep works their own portfolio.

story.title: Managing the sales floor before month-end
paragraphs: Team leads can see whether each rep is on pace for the month, which stores still need outreach and who is on shift to cover them. They can coach a rep on their next promotion or direct outreach toward an overlooked group of merchants.

The sales claims pilot also distinguishes work awaiting review from approved wins. For pricing work, the Hub tracks whether a merchant’s lower menu markup held for 30 days. That gives a lead a basis for coaching on the outcome of the offer as well as the initial sale.

story.title: Sales figures leadership can explain
paragraphs: In the weekly account management review, analysts can compare approved sales claims with official results by product, then examine each team’s figures. Reporting leads publish the current week’s figures straight to the Google Sheets workbook leadership already uses. That removes the step of copying totals by hand.
We also separated who owns an account today from who earned a sale. If a rep moves teams on Friday, Tuesday’s sale still counts for the team that earned it.

projects.name: Train RAG SemanticSearch

projects.name: Hypothetical Document Embeddings
projects.summary: A notebook exploring how a generated example answer can help retrieve relevant passages from hotel reviews.

projects.name: US Census Demographic Data
projects.summary: Built two Tableau dashboards and a visual story from 2015 US county data to explore population, poverty and transportation.
details: Documented the design decisions behind each view and compared poverty with unemployment across counties.

projects.name: No Show Appointments
projects.summary: Explored more than 100,000 medical appointments in Brazil to identify patterns in attendance.
details: Used pandas and Matplotlib to examine appointment histories and characteristics associated with missed visits.

projects.name: Explore US Bikeshare Data
projects.summary: Compared trip duration, popular stations and travel times across Chicago, New York City and Washington, DC.
details: Wrote a Python program to calculate descriptive statistics from each city's bike share records.

projects.name: Query a Digital Music Store

details: Queried a relational music store database to examine media sales and purchasing behavior.
